title: Optimal Metric-Aware Class Rebalancing in Federated Learning

problem.claim: Class imbalance in federated learning is worsened by global data imbalance and local heterogeneity across clients, while effective mitigation must respect privacy constraints.

gap.claim: Existing class rebalancing ratios largely depend on empirical results rather than an analytical determination.

contributions.claim: An analytical class rebalancing method computes optimal rebalancing ratios for imbalanced datasets.
The method theoretically derives relationships between macro-precision, macro-recall, macro-F1, and the rebalancing ratio.
An efficient algorithm determines the rebalancing ratio that maximizes the corresponding evaluation metrics.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that this is the first analytical and parameter-free solution to the problem.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The method is parameter-free and does not increase the complexity of existing neural models.
The authors report that the method achieves the optimum ratio for the concerned metrics while maintaining low computational complexity that scales linearly with the number of clients and samples.
Experiments on different datasets are reported to validate the effectiveness of the algorithms.

narrative_sequence.summary: Federated learning faces class imbalance from global imbalance and client heterogeneity, with privacy constraints making mitigation difficult.
Common rebalancing approaches select ratios empirically.
The paper derives metric–ratio relationships and uses them to compute optimal ratios with an efficient algorithm.
The method is described as parameter-free, complexity-preserving, and linearly scaling with clients and samples.
Experiments on different datasets are reported as validating algorithm effectiveness.

source_observation.claim: The method analytically links rebalancing ratios to macro-precision, macro-recall, and macro-F1.

interpretation.claim: Metric-aware rebalancing can replace empirically selected ratios when the relevant metric relationships are analytically characterizable.

application.claim: For privacy-constrained federated classification, consider selecting class weights by deriving their effect on the target evaluation metric.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish applicability beyond the described imbalanced federated classification setting or metrics.

unknowns: Datasets, baselines, metric values, and experimental settings are not specified.
The analytical derivation, algorithm details, privacy mechanism, and optimality conditions are not provided.
